summary.title: Calibration Window Counter
summary.statement_md:
A weather station records daily temperature changes as an array of integers, where a positive value means warming and a negative value means cooling. Engineers calibrate their equipment every time a stretch of consecutive days sums to an exact multiple of a cycle length m (a sum of exactly 0 also counts).

Given the array `nums` and the integer `m`, return the number of contiguous subarrays whose total change is divisible by `m`.

summary.title: Tower Range Scanner
summary.statement_md:
Towers stand along a highway at distinct positions, given as a sorted array `towers` (strictly increasing). You are given a list of `queries`, each `[position, radius]`, describing a car parked at `position` whose detector reaches towers within `radius` (inclusive) in either direction.

For every query, count how many towers fall within `[position - radius, position + radius]`. Return the counts as an array, in the same order as the queries.

summary.title: Sensor Burst Window
summary.statement_md:
A sensor feed is recorded as an array of positive integer readings `nums`. Find the shortest contiguous window whose readings sum to at least `min_sum` **and** that contains at least `min_distinct` different reading values.

Return the length of that shortest window. If no contiguous window satisfies both conditions at once, return 0.

summary.title: Locked Doors Shortest Path
summary.statement_md:
A facility has `n` rooms numbered 0..n-1 connected by two-way corridors. Some corridors are open passageways that cost no time to cross; others are locked doors that take exactly one minute to unlock and pass through.

You are given `n`, a list of corridors `edges` (each `[u, v, w]`, where `w = 0` means open and `w = 1` means locked), a `start` room, and an `end` room.

Return the minimum total minutes needed to travel from `start` to `end`, or `-1` if `end` is unreachable.

summary.title: Sensor Glitch Recovery
summary.statement_md:
A weather station logged daily temperature changes for `n` days, some negative. You want to choose one contiguous block of days that maximizes the total change.

The station had one faulty sensor day at most, so within your chosen block you may discard (remove) at most one reading before summing — the remaining readings must still form the same block minus that one day, and at least one reading must remain.

Given the readings, return the maximum total achievable.

summary.title: Warehouse Scan Batches
summary.statement_md:
A warehouse conveyor scans item IDs in a fixed sequence `ids`. For an audit, the sequence must be cut into consecutive batches so that every occurrence of a given item ID falls entirely inside one batch — no ID may appear in two different batches.

Split the sequence into the maximum possible number of such batches. Return the length of each batch, listed in the order the batches occur along the sequence.
